articleTitle: A 21 GHZ Reflection Amplifier MMIC for Retro-Directive Antenna and RFID Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: In this work a novel MMIC reflection amplifier is presented which is capable of more than 10 dB return gain and operates at K band. The amplifier occupies an area of only 1.5 mm times 2 mm and has been fabricated using OMMIC D01PH process technology. The fabricated die has been successfully connected to a 50 Omega K band horn antenna as well as to a compact patch antenna. Return gain above 14 dB and above 7.5 dB has been measured when a transmitted signal is incident upon the horn and patch systems respectively

articleTitle: Millimetre Wave Antennas for Vehicle Telematics
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: The goal of a completely autonomous vehicular system is being approached through the use of telematics involving the transmission and reception of information in the 63-64 GHz band. This will consist of vehicle to vehicle communications as well as communications with roadside beacons placed at intermittent and strategic locations. In addition, automotive radar will be applied in the 77 GHz band. At BAE Systems ATC, low cost technology has been applied to the design of antennas for both vehicular telemetry and automotive radar. We present a review of antennas for 60 GHz application using low cost approaches such as microstrip technology and discuss measured and predicted results. In addition, we examine integration of antenna technologies for future automotive applications

articleTitle: Integrated Heterodyne Receivers for MM & SubMM Atmospheric Remote Sensing
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: Methods to increase the sensitivity, level of integration, and design robustness of low-cost integrated elements for millimetre and sub-millimetre receiver arrays are presented. This is illustrated in reference to the MARSCHALS airborne limb sounding instrument. Recent developments in photomixing elements to generate a millimetre wave signal are described. The design, fabrication and test of a fixed-tuned 380 GHz Schottky-based receiver are also presented. This incorporates a high-power frequency doubler to the ISO-200 GHz range and a 360-400 GHz sub-harmonic Schottky diode mixer which exhibits state-of-the-art sensitivity

articleTitle: Design considerations for a millimetric front-end for FMCW radar
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: This paper describes the architecture and design considerations for a high performance millimetric front end for the Tarsierreg T1100 runway debris monitoring system radar. Tarsier T1100 is a FMCW radar dedicated for the detection of very small debris on airport runways and has been designed with no compromise in performance. Measured results are presented for different environmental scenarios and their impact on the various performance parameters of the front-end is discussed

articleTitle: Si Based UWB Radar Sensors - Design, Development, and Production
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: Automotive short-range sensor networks at 24 GHz represent the first truly high volume commercial system at mm-wave, with first year production quantities already eclipsing previous products such as autonomous cruise control (ACC), and the various microwave radio networks (e.g. LMDS). The emphasis on product quality, reliability, cost, and performance demanded by automotive OEMs has meant that an innovative approach to product development, packaging, and test has had to be introduced to mm-wave products. This paper will highlight some of the key technical hurdles and their solutions in the development and introduction to production of a 24 GHz UWB radar sensor based on custom-designed SiGe ICs

articleTitle: Development of Millimetre-Wave Radar Products
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: This paper describes the development of a range of millimetre-wave radar products for autonomous cruise control (ACC), altimeter, and industrial sensing applications. By applying the development approach used in the development of high volume radio products, the cost of the both the development and the end products have been kept as low as possible

articleTitle: Metawaveguide Resonator Structures for Millimetre Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to investigate a novel class of metawaveguide resonator structure using S-shaped SRR for use at mm-wave, submm-wave and terahertz frequencies. It aims to show that this type of resonator can be easily realized with a single metalo-dielectric insert within rectangular waveguide. The simulated results for air-filled metal pipe half-wavelength rectangular waveguide resonator and resonator structure using S-shaped SRR at 57 GHz, 59 Ghz and 64 GHz are presented

articleTitle: Hand-Held Microwave Search Detector
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: This paper describes the development of a patented, novel, low cost, microwave search detector using noise radar technology operating in the 27-40 GHz range of frequencies, initially reported in SPIE 2004. Experiments have shown that plastic explosives, ceramics and plastic material hidden on the body can be detected with the system. This paper considers the basic physics of the technique and reports on the development of an initial prototype system for hand search of suspects. The radar uses a novel lens system and the design and modelling of this for optimum depth of field of focus will be reported

articleTitle: Packaging and MMIC Design for Low Cost MM-Wave Modules
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: MM-wave subsystems have traditionally been produced in low volumes and at high cost due to circuit and substrate costs and limited repeatability of module manufacture. Advances in MMIC processing, packaging technologies and modelling techniques are potentially enabling mm-wave modules to be procured at reasonable cost. This paper summarises packaging and MMIC designs at QinetiQ above 60 GHz aimed at using low cost manufacturing techniques. By way of example two applications are considered; a mm-wave radio link at around 60 GHz and a 94 GHz receiver for imaging applications

articleTitle: Low Cost MMICS for Automotive Radar and Passive Radiometric Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: TriQuint has developed power amplifiers, filters, duplexers, switches, phase shifters, and frequency conversion components specifically for systems ranging from RF-frequency cellular handsets, millimeter-wave frequency point-to-point radio transceivers, automotive radar and passive imaging applications. This paper presents TriQuint's latest MMIC developments for 77-81 GHz automotive radar and 94 GHz passive imaging markets on low cost 4 and 6 inch VPIN, HBT, pHEMT and mHEMT production processes

articleTitle: Monolithic Millimetrewave Integrated Circuits (MMICs) issues beyond 100GHz for High Resolution Imaging and Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: In this work we will present the effect of parasitic moding on the mm-wave G-Band (140-220 GHz) performance of coplanar waveguide (CPW) components on GaAs substrates as a function of substrate thickness and layout geometries. It is observed that mm-wave energy leakage especially at 220 GHz is quite significant, i.e. as high as 9 dB for a standard short structure fabricated on 630 mum

articleTitle: Advancements in MM-Wave On-Wafer S-Parameter Verification
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: The paper presents new on-wafer probe capabilities which offer improved measurement repeatability and calibration accuracy in the WR-10 through WR-5 waveguide bands. New types of membrane probe tips to 220 GHz and new customized impedance standard substrates have been developed. These elements are incorporated in a family of wafer probes with improved repeatability and accuracy throughout the waveguide bands. Measured results will be presented in the paper

articleTitle: Optimising the Design of 77GHz LNAs
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: Many new application areas for MMICs are appearing at higher millimeter wave frequencies, which require high volume, low cost MMIC designs. In these cases, it is essential to optimize the whole of system, including all the electromagnetic effects that can compromise the design. Ansoft have teamed with UMS to develop a next generation design kit for MMIC design. The poster presentation illustrates how this design kit has been used to optimize a 77 GHz LNA for automotive applications including the advantages of utilizing the design kit for co-design of the active and passive elements of circuit and system, as well as how the tools can easily be used to compute and compare design trade offs

articleTitle: Low Cost Implementation of an ACC Automotive Radar
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: This paper will identify some of the key measurement requirements demanded of an automotive radar system. It will then explore the challenges required to make such a precision measuring device at a cost that can be afforded by the mass automotive market. The challenges that will be touched on to produce such a low cost adaptive cruise control (ACC) radar will include: radar modulation techniques, microwave oscillator configuration, and mechanical antenna structures. Having developed such a radar TRW is now applying this radar as a key component in its range of active safety products. A summary of the range of safety products that can be implemented with such radar technology is identified

articleTitle: Passive and Active MM-Wave People Screening Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: A passive mm-wave people screening imager is discussed. Frames extracted from video sequences are presented showing good detection of threat objects. Active imaging based on an FMCW concept is discussed and some initial images presented

articleTitle: MM-Wave Super Harmonic Injection Locked Frequency Dividers
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: This paper describes the design of a mm-wave super-harmonic injection locked (SHIL) analogue frequency divide-by-2 circuit. The technique exploits the case whereby a saturated amplifier can become unstable and oscillate at exactly half the input frequency. This particular design example operates at an input frequency of 35 GHz, but the technique is viable to frequencies approaching the Fmax of the amplifier transistor

articleTitle: Simulation Technology for Efficient Millimeter-Wave IC Development
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: Development of millimeter-wave integrated circuits - and, thus, systems at moderate cost depends strongly on circuit simulation software. The demands placed on such software by design at millimeter wavelengths are much greater than those at the lower microwave frequencies. At the same time, the relatively high cost of testing and "tweaking" millimeter circuits, their lower yield, and the need for advanced technologies, makes such software an especially critical part of a practical, low-cost design flow. This paper discusses the requirements of such software and describes the ways in which improvements in both simulation technology and basic software technology have made efficient millimeter-wave circuit design possible

articleTitle: High Performance MM-Wave Radar Techniques
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on MM-Wave Products and Technologies
abstract: The Millimetre Wave and High-Field ESR Group at St Andrews has recently been developing a range of mm-wave radar technologies that have yielded the successful development of various advanced prototype systems exhibiting state-of-the-art performance, which are reviewed here. These include a long-range, high resolution FMCW imaging radar for volcano mapping, and a nanosecond pulsed, coherent, radar-like system developed for spectroscopy
